Package org.geysermc.paletter.internal.behaviour

Class BehaviourStore

java.lang.Object
org.geysermc.paletter.internal.behaviour.BehaviourStore
@Internal public final class BehaviourStore extends Object
The behaviour values of vanilla blocks and items of every version, each stored once. Immutable.

A capture is what one source said about one data version: the block states (by state hash) and items (by identifier) it covers and, per key, their values. Captures are kept in application order: by version, and within a version the weaker source first. A capture stores only the values that differ from what the captures before it resolve to, so a value is stored once for all the versions it stays the same in.

The value of a key for an id in version v: the last capture of a version up to v that covers the id decides, with the value it stored, else the value it confirmed (the one before it). That capture is the provenance; a version without such a capture of its own inherits the value, visibly (Provenance.inherited()).

The bundled form is behaviour.nbt, gzipped big endian NBT: 

 format: int                       2
 versions: [string], protocols: int[]   oldest first
 captures: [{version, source, reference, base: int, blocks_added: int[], blocks_removed: int[], items_added: [string], items_removed: [string]}]
                                   coverage as a change to capture base (an earlier one of the same source; -1: none)
 shapes: [[float]]                 every distinct shape once, six floats per box
 blocks: {key: [{capture: int, mask?: byte[], values}]}   mask: a bit per id the capture covers (sorted), set if
                                   the column has a value for it; no mask: every covered id
 items: {key: [{capture: int, mask?: byte[], values}]}
 postprocessed: [{key, capture, ids, note}]   the capture's values of these ids were post-processed by its source
 disputes: [{key, capture, alt_capture, ids, values}]   another capture of the same version said values for
                                   these ids while the capture decided; nothing direct from BDS settled it
 defaults: [{key, source, reference, values: [one]}]   the BDS default of custom content without the component
 metadata: {...}                   what generated the file and from which sources (informational)
 _generated: string                who wrote the file; readers ignore it, tests check it
Values by key type: float list, int array, byte array (booleans), string list, int array of shape indexes.
